Liam (acme): Hey team — over the last ~30m our EU users are seeing huge p95 latency and a few 403s. We've got a spike in tokens billed and some requests showing X-Region: eu-west but the response headers look like they're served from us-west. Can you check?

Maya (support): Thanks Liam, I'm looking. Can you paste a failing request id or a raw curl? Any request_id from response headers helps.

Liam (acme): example request_id: req_0a9b3f. Sample curl: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"open-redwood-1","input":"hi"}'` — got 403 and `X-Serving-Pool: hosted-us-west`. Latency ~700ms.

Maya (support): Got it. I'm escalating to SRE. @Zane can you pull routing logs for req_0a9b3f and check pin state for acme's dedicated pool?

Zane (sre): Looking — there's a pattern. Around 1835121000 we had a routing-policy flip in canary that loosened dedicated-pin enforcement for fallbacks (tag: fallback: allow-hosted). For requests arriving with stale pin TTL the router was allowed to fall back to hosted rather than queue/retry. I see `req_0a9b3f` shows `X-Pin-Region: eu-west-1` but `pin_state: stale` and `route_decision: hosted-us-west`.

Zane (sre): Paste of relevant logs (trimmed):
```
[1835124320] req=0a9b3f client=acme region_hint=eu-west-1 pin_state=STALE route=hosted-us-west fallback_reason=pin_ttl_expired routing_policy=canary-2026-03-17
[1835124320] token_cost=125 tokens latency_ms=680
```

Maya (support): BillingBot is also showing a hosted usage spike attributed to acme — Billing Ops, can you confirm if this looks like a cross-region overflow billed at hosted rates?

BillingBot: Confirmed. The last 45m show ~2.3M tokens billed on hosted for account acme (unexpected). Estimated overage ~+$1.2k.

Ana (acctmgmt): Oof. We'll prep credits if it's a platform regression. Waiting on SRE root cause.

Zane (sre): Root cause summary: 1) recent routing-policy canary changed fallback semantics to prefer availability over pin strictness. 2) For a subset of dedicated pools the pin TTL isn't being refreshed on certain long-held connections (bug in pin-refresh worker). 3) Combo caused requests from EU to fall through to hosted-us-west creating extra latency and unexpected hosted billing.

Maya (support): Repro steps for SRE/devs:
1) Use a dedicated customer with pinned eu-west pool.
2) Force pin TTL to expire (`/internal/pin/expire?customer=acme`).
3) Send 100 concurrent requests with `X-Client-Region: eu-west-1`.
4) Observe `route_decision` header and `X-Serving-Pool`. Expectation: should have retried/queued to dedicated for 30s; actual: immediate hosted fallback.

Zane (sre): I ran the repro. Quick command I used:
```
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" https://router.redwood.internal/v1/proxy?model=open-redwood-1 &
done
```
Observed 78% immediate hosted routing when pin TTL expired.

dev-deploy-bot: Deploy event: canary routing-policy v2026-03-17 pushed at 1835121000 by eng-runtime. Rollback possible via `deploy rollback canary-2026-03-17`.

Zane (sre): Action items (short):
- Revert canary routing-policy immediately (rollback via deploy-bot).
- Patch pin-refresh worker to aggressively refresh TTL for connections >5m.
- Add metric alert on "hosted-bypass_rate" per customer > 1% over baseline.
- Work with billing to reconcile and issue credits.

Maya (support): Rolling back policy now. @dev-deploy-bot please start rollback.

dev-deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for canary-2026-03-17 at 1835125200. Progress: 12/12 nodes rollback complete.

Zane (sre): After rollback I'm seeing new routing decisions for recent reqs go to dedicated eu-west. Latency back to ~90ms. No new hosted billing for acme in last 10m.

Maya (support): Maya -> Liam: Sorry for the incident, root cause is the canary policy + pin refresh bug. We're issuing billing credits and the routing-policy has been rolled back. We'll follow up with a postmortem and ETA on a permanent fix.

Liam (acme): Thanks for the quick response. Can you share the postmortem and the billing credit details when available? Also would like opt-in to stricter pin enforcement for our account until fixed.

Maya (support): Agree — we'll set an account-level override to require strict-pin for acme until the fix is released. I'll DM you details and put the postmortem link here when ready. :thumbsup:

BillingBot: Created ticket BILL-8943 for reconciliation/credit for acme. Owner: billing-ops.

ops-oncall-bot: Alert cleared: hosted-bypass_rate(acme) back to baseline at 1835127800.

Zane (sre): Follow-ups: PR for pin-refresh fix (in review), add integ test to ensure fallback respects strict-pin header, and add runbook steps to check `pin_state` and `route_decision` headers for customer escalations.

Maya (support): Closing thread for now — reopening if Liam sees anything else. Thanks all.
